S70.01.note: Single-instance and crash-recovery screen code was not located by visible words; the earlier recovery check was not re-verified.
steps: Open AGI Desktop from the Applications folder.
Open AGI Desktop a second time and check that the one open window comes forward instead of a second copy appearing.
Close the window with the red button, then click the app icon in the Dock and check the same window returns.
S70.01.where: Effect seen by opening and re-opening the app window

S70.02.note: The Help menu uses the system role, so its title comes from macOS, not a literal string.
steps: Click File in the menu bar and check the items listed: New Chat, New Temporary Chat, New Project, Open Folder.
Click Edit and check Undo, Redo, Cut, Copy, Paste, Find.
Click View and History, then Window and Help, and check each lists its items.
Click File > New Chat and check a new chat opens. Compare with Expected.
S70.02.where: Menu bar > File > New Chat (menu titles File, Edit, View, History, Window, Help)

S70.03.note: Open Desktop and Quit labels are built from a template, so their literal text was not found; the Menu bar hint is Show Desktop in the menu bar.
steps: Click the AGI Desktop icon in the menu bar.
Check the items: Open Desktop, New Chat, Quick Ask, Screenshot to Chat, Dictation, Shortcuts, Check for Updates, Quit.
Click Shortcuts and check the shortcut choices list.
Open Settings > Desktop app > General, find the Menu bar switch, turn it off, and check the icon disappears from the menu bar.
S70.03.where: Menu bar icon (AGI Desktop) > Open Desktop; > New Chat; > Quick Ask; > Screenshot to Chat; > Dictation; > Shortcuts

S70.04.note: Behaviour is in the app code (activate and window-all-closed handlers); no visible label on the control itself.
steps: Open a chat window and click the red close button at the top left.
Look at the Dock: the AGI Desktop icon should still be there with its running dot.
Click the AGI Desktop icon in the Dock.
Check the chat window comes back. Compare with Expected.
S70.04.where: Red close button on the window, then the AGI Desktop icon in the Dock

S70.05.note: Conflict notes come from STATUS_NOTE in the same file.
steps: Open Settings, choose the Desktop app group, then General.
Find the row Quick Ask shortcut and open its dropdown.
Pick another choice, or No shortcut.

Click into another app and press the chosen key combination; check Quick Ask opens. For a conflict, check the note under the row: Already used by another Desktop shortcut or Already used by another app.
S70.05.where: Settings > Desktop app > General > Quick Ask shortcut (dropdown)

S70.06.note: The send control was not confirmed by visible words; the Quick Ask page is apps/web/app/quick-ask/page.tsx.
steps: From any other app, press the Quick Ask shortcut, or click File > Quick Ask in AGI Desktop.
Check a small window opens above the other windows.
Type a short prompt in the box and send it.
Check the answer appears in the small window.
S70.06.where: File > Quick Ask (or the Quick Ask shortcut from any app)

S70.07.note: Searched apps/desktop/electron and apps/web/features/desktop-host for companion; only a code comment in apps/desktop/electron/quickAsk.ts mentions companion windows. The nearest control is Quick Ask (floating window) and Window > Always on Top.

S70.08.note: The item is greyed out when the front window cannot take the setting.
steps: Open a chat window and click Window in the menu bar.
Click Always on Top so it shows a tick.
Click into another app such as Notes or Finder.
Check the AGI window stays above the other windows. Click Always on Top again to turn it off.

S70.09.note: Move Conversation is greyed out unless a conversation is in the front window.
steps: Click Window > New Window and check a second AGI window opens.
Open a conversation in one window.
Click Window > Move Conversation to New Window.
Check the conversation opens in its own window and the old window no longer shows it. Compare with Expected.
S70.09.where: Window > New Window; Window > Move Conversation to New Window

S70.11.note: Only the folder path was confirmed as the OS dialog (the shell owns the directory dialog); the file picker path was not checked.
steps: Click File > Open Folder in the menu bar.
Check the operating system's own folder dialog opens.
Choose a folder and click Open.
Check a notice says which folder was approved.
S70.11.where: File > Open Folder (folder dialog); composer + > Add photos & files (file picker)

S70.12.note: Local access is rendered by Settings > Capabilities (apps/web/features/settings/sections/CapabilitiesSection.tsx).
steps: Approve a folder with File > Open Folder.
Open Settings, click Capabilities, and scroll to Local access.
Quit AGI Desktop with Cmd+Q, reopen it, and return to Settings > Capabilities.
Check the folder is still listed under Folders. Click Remove access in the confirmation to revoke it, then check it disappears.

S70.13.needs: an approved folder and a file inside it
S70.13.note: The assistant-side search (device-steps) was not tested from chat; only the person's dialog path was traced.
steps: In a new chat click the + button in the composer and click Attach from local folder.
In the dialog Attach from a local folder, open an approved folder.
Type a file name or some text in the box Search names and text and click Search.
Check the results under Matching names and Matching text.

S70.14.needs: an approved folder and a Desktop build
S70.14.note: The approval prompt wording was not located by visible words.
steps: In a new chat click + and choose Add working folder, then pick an approved folder.
Type: Create a file named test.txt in this folder with the word hello.
Check a permission prompt appears before anything is written.
Approve it and check the file exists in the folder in Finder.
S70.14.where: Composer + > Add working folder, then ask the assistant in chat

S70.15.needs: an approved folder and a Desktop build
S70.15.note: No sandboxing text was found in LocalAccessSection, so sandboxing could not be checked from the labels.
steps: In a chat with an approved folder, click + and choose Run a local command.
Type a harmless command such as ls and send it.
Check an approval request appears before the command runs.
Approve it and check the output streams into the chat. Settings > Capabilities > Local access shows the Commands section.

S70.19.note: The window-capture variant is Window to Chat, set in the Desktop app settings.
steps: Click File > Screenshot to Chat in the menu bar.
Choose the screen to capture if asked.
Check the screenshot is attached in the chat composer.
Send it and check the image appears in the conversation.

S70.21.needs: Accessibility and Screen Recording permission on macOS, and a Desktop build
S70.21.note: The Any app label is in ComputerUseSettings.tsx, which is one of the Desktop app settings pages.
steps: Open Settings, click the Desktop app group, then Computer use, and turn on Any app.
Ask the assistant in chat to click something on screen, and approve when asked.
Check the control bar labelled Computer use appears with Take over or Hand back and Stop.
Click Take over, then Stop, and check the assistant stops moving the pointer.
S70.21.where: Settings > Desktop app > Computer use (turn on Any app); then the control bar shows Take over, Hand back, Stop

S70.22.needs: a phone and a Desktop build
S70.22.note: The section returns nothing unless the desktop host is present and supported; a hidden-in-v1 setting was not checked in code.
steps: Open Settings and click Capabilities.
Scroll to Remote Control.
Click Pair a phone and check a pairing code and QR code appear.
Scan the code with the phone and check Connected to appears.
S70.22.where: Settings > Capabilities > Remote Control > Pair a phone

S70.24.needs: a Desktop build and a restart
S70.24.note: The macOS app menu also has Launch at Login (apps/desktop/electron/appMenu.ts).
steps: Open Settings, click Desktop app, then General.
Turn on the switch Run on startup.
Quit AGI Desktop and log out and back in, or restart the Mac.
Check AGI Desktop opens by itself. Turn the switch off to stop it.
S70.24.where: Settings > Desktop app > General > Run on startup

labels.text: Nothing is running in the background.

S70.25.needs: a running agent or background task
S70.25.note: The Keep computer awake switch is also in General and is a separate control.
steps: Start an agent task in a chat so something runs in the background.
Open Settings, click Desktop app, then General.
Find the section Running on this Mac and check it lists the running item.
Click Stop next to it and check Nothing is running in the background appears.
S70.25.where: Settings > Desktop app > General > Running on this Mac

S70.26.needs: a Desktop build; a newer published version to see the update path
S70.26.note: The UI asks for one click to download and then relaunch; it does not show a silent install, unlike Expected's by itself wording. Help menu also has Check for Updates (apps/desktop/electron/appMenu.ts).
steps: Open Settings, click Desktop app, then General.
Find the row App version and click Check for updates.
If a newer version exists, check the button changes to Download installer, then Relaunch to update.
If none exists, check This is the latest version appears.
S70.26.where: Settings > Desktop app > General > App version > Check for updates

S70.28.note: Clear Cache and Restart is also under Troubleshooting; do not click it unless intended.
steps: Click Help in the menu bar and hover Troubleshooting.
Click Copy Diagnostics.
Paste into a text field (Cmd+V) and check diagnostic text appears.
Go back to Help > Troubleshooting and click Open Logs, and check the log folder opens.
S70.28.where: Help > Troubleshooting > Copy Diagnostics (or Open Logs)

S70.29.note: The Storage page is shown only in the Electron host.
steps: Open Settings, click Desktop app, then Storage.
Check the heading Storage and the row Data folder show what is kept on the computer.
Under Clean up, click Clear for the web cache or Delete for old logs, then confirm.
Check the size goes down and the confirmation text Chats stay on this computer appears where chats are kept.

S70.30.needs: a Desktop build and a link to open
S70.30.note: Accepted link paths are in apps/web/features/desktop-host/lib/deep-links.ts; the exact paths were not tested.
steps: In Notes or Safari, open a link that starts with agiworkforce-cloud://.
Check AGI Desktop opens or comes forward.
Check it lands on the same screen the link names, such as a chat.
Click a notification the app raised and check it opens that conversation.
S70.30.where: Open an agiworkforce-cloud:// link from another app, such as Notes or Safari

S70.31.needs: a Desktop build and at least one saved answer
S70.31.note: Remove button label was not found by visible words; the control is rendered by the card at DesktopPermissionsSection.tsx:175-180.
steps: Open Settings, click Desktop app, then General, and scroll to Permissions.
Read Your answers and the system hint about computer use, screenshots and dictation.
Click Open System Settings to check the macOS privacy pane opens.
Click Remove on an answer and check it is gone, so Desktop asks again next time. Click Refresh to reload.
